text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Sunday's Pakistani newspapers:

- Pakistan and the United States have signed a memorandum of understanding, agreeing to set up a U.S.-Pakistan Buisness Development Forum, U.S. Assistant Secretary of Commerce Raymond Vickery told a news conference in Islamabad on Saturday.

- Pakistani officials said on Saturday a war-like situation existed along the Line of Control dividing Kashmir between India and Pakistan as two sides traded artillery and machinegun fire while controversial elections were being held in the Indian-ruled part of the disputed region.
- Presidents of Pakistan's three stock exchanges will meet Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday to discuss ways to improve the prevailing situation in the stock market.
- Marches and public rallies were held throughout Azad Kashmir on Saturday to protest against controversial elections in Indian-ruled Kashmir.

- The Pakistani government has shelved the proposal to give concessions in general sales tax (GST) and the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry and exporters have been asked to wait for the implementation of the proposal at some opportune time. The proposal has been deferred because International Monetary Fund officials are due to visit Pakistan and they will never agree to any change in the GST.
- Pakistan cement plant owners have demanded incentives to export cement.
- Agriculture Minister Yousuf Talpur says cotton production target of 10 million 375-lb bales will be met.
- The government has resolved a dispute with Motorola Inc of the United States to allow it to resume cellular telephone services in Karachi, U.S. Assistant Secretary of Commerce Raymond Vickery said.
- Pakistan is the 18th most indebted country in the world with its total external debt standing at a staggering $29.57 billion, according to the recently released World Debt Tables.

- Depreciation of the Pakistani rupee is likely to continue until the dispute with the International Monetary Fund regarding the release of standby loan instalments is settled, sources in the Ministry of Finance say.
